items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to providing insurance corporations with a tax credit for investments made in rural business growth funds; and to amend the state finance law, in relation to establishing the New York agriculture and rural jobs fund
items.lawCode: Add §§43 & 187-t, amd §§1511 & 210-B, Tax L; add §99-aa, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4727

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the tax law, in relation to
providing insurance corporations with a tax credit for investments
made in rural business growth funds; and to amend the state finance
law, in relation to establishing the New York agriculture and rural
jobs fund

 PURPOSE :

To allow insurance corporations to receive a tax credit for investing
in rural business growth funds and to establish a fund dedicated to
the well-being of New York Agriculture and Rural Jobs.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 amends section 43 of the tax law to define "affiliate,"
"closing date," "credit-eligible capital contribution," "eligible
investment authority," a business's "principle business operations,"
"rural area," "rural business concern," "rural business growth fund,"
"rural growth investment," "taxable year," and the processes for
granting and revoking certification for the tax credit, and implements
a system for reporting business progress.

Section 2 adds subdivision (dd) to section 1511 of the tax law,
allowing taxpayers to receive a tax credit for certain investments to
a rural business growth fund.

Section 3 amends section 187-t of the tax law to allow taxpayers to
receive a tax credit for certain investments made to a rural business
growth fund.

Section 4 adds subdivision 52 to section 210-B of the tax law,
allowing taxpayers to receive a tax credit for certain investments to
a rural business growth fund.

Section 5 amends section 99-aa of the finance law to establish and
define the New York agriculture and rural jobs fund.

Section 6 establishes the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The agricultural lands of New York's farmlands have been identified as
a critical component of the state's efforts to conserve open space,
protecting agricultural production, scenic areas, and vital wildlife
habitats.

This bill establishes a fund to help promote and sustain the economies
of New York's rural communities and protect the jobs of hardworking
individuals in these areas.

This bill also provides an incentive for taxpayers to invest in the
established fund, supporting the economic development of New York's
rural lands and the state as a whole.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect July 1, 2017.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 266
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 4727-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the tax law, in relation to providing insurance
      corporations with a tax credit for investments made in rural busi-
      ness growth funds; and to amend the state finance law, in relation
      to establishing the New York agriculture and rural jobs fund"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill seeks to create a tax credit for insurance  corporations  to
ostensibly  invest  in  rural jobs for an unbudgeted cost of $65 million
and fundamentally jeopardizes the federal treatment of New York's  fran-
chise  tax. Specifically, this bill seeks to establish a fund for insur-
ance corporations to invest in rural businesses or businesses  in  rural
areas,  and would also provide franchise tax credits to those who invest
in such a fund. Insurance corporations that invest  in  the  fund  would
also  receive  a credit against the tax imposed by Ins. L. Section 1112,
which is a retaliatory tax imposed on  an  insurance  company  domiciled
outside  of  New York State when that company's home state imposes taxes
(and fees, penalties and fines) against New York insurers that are high-
er than those imposed upon that company by New York.
 
  The bill's stated goal to promote jobs in rural areas  is  a  laudable
one,  but  the  bill  faces  insurmountable legal, technical, and fiscal
problems that make it impossible to sign. The  bill  sets  forth  overly
broad  criteria  to  target  businesses for investment, ambiguous credit
claiming provisions, and an ineffective credit recapture structure.  The
bill would also jeopardize the federal treatment of New York's corporate
taxes  as  non-discriminatory  franchise  taxes by allowing investors to
avoid paying fixed dollar minimum taxes. Taxpayers subject to  franchise
taxes  must  pay  at  least a minimum amount of tax for the privilege of
doing business in the State. This concept is vital to maintaining  these
taxes  as  non-discriminatory  franchise  taxes. Because this bill would
allow corporations to reduce their tax to zero in any year, the  classi-
fication  of  a tax as a franchise tax would be jeopardized, potentially
putting at risk millions of dollars of State franchise tax revenue.
 
  This bill would also have  significant  fiscal  implications  for  the
State.    While the bill's cap on investments theoretically would have a
total fiscal cost of $65 million, the cost could escalate  further.  Any
new program with a fiscal impact of this magnitude needs to be addressed
in  the  context  of  State  budget  negotiations  as part of an overall
economic development strategy for rural and agricultural jobs.
 
  I am strongly committed to promoting and investing in New York's agri-
culture and rural communities to benefit residents and businesses alike,
including the establishment of the New Farmers Grant  Program,  the  $10
million Job Development Authority Agriculture Loan Fund, the Small Busi-
ness Revolving Loan Fund, the New York State Capital Access Program, the
Innovate New York Fund, the NYS Innovation Venture Capital Fund, the Job
Development  Authority  Direct  Loan Program, the Upstate Revitalization
Initiative, and the Excelsior Jobs Program. I lowered the  tax  rate  on
 
corporate  income  for upstate qualified manufacturers to zero, provided
enhanced funding for  rural  public  transportation  projects,  enhanced
funding to the State's Farmland Protection Implementation Grants Program
to  support  conservation  easement  projects on dairy farms, and made a
$500 million broadband  investment  to  ensure  rural  communities  have
access to high speed internet.
 
  I  will  continue  to support initiatives that promote and sustain the
economies of New York's rural communities. Thus, while I am  constrained
to  veto  this  bill,  I look forward to working with the Legislature to
develop a program that meets this bill's  stated  purpose  of  improving
rural and agricultural jobs.
 
  This bill is disapproved.                   (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
